items.title: When web search is down
items.text: If web search fails, the researcher writes RESEARCH.md from what it knows (and says so) instead of searching in circles; if it ends with no RESEARCH.md, the chat is told plainly.

releases.title: The chat starts after the research

items.title: No more stopping before it starts
items.text: A stop from an earlier request no longer ends a new /crew at once (it said Stopped. and the researcher worked on alone). The researcher aims for about 3 minutes, and the chat starts after 5 at most.

items.title: Background agents update live
items.text: The Background agents list redraws as soon as an agent does something, and its times move every second; before, it only changed when you clicked or typed.

items.title: Click into a background agent
items.text: In /crew, click an agent under Background agents to watch it live in the conversation's place: what it writes, each step and its result, the files it changes, command output and errors. Esc goes back to the chat.

items.title: A researcher starts every /crew
items.text: /crew now always begins with a researcher on Ultra Flash, shown under Background agents: it researches the topic (how it works, its real numbers, how it is usually built, the pitfalls, a checklist) and writes RESEARCH.md; the main chat starts once it is done, with its report and the notes to read.

items.title: The watcher steps in less
items.text: It only looks at an agent yAI's own counters show looping (the same step 3 times in its last 12, a file changed back and forth, the same reasoning again, refused repeats), waits 3 minutes between instructions to the same agent, and blocks only after an instruction was ignored. /team's watcher waits 3 minutes too.

items.title: Cut-off tool calls
items.text: A tool call cut off by the reply's length limit used to arrive with no arguments (write_file with no path, again and again); it now keeps what it can and reads as cut off, so the agent is told to write the file in parts.

items.title: A chat with background agents
items.text: /crew <task> is now this chat itself, with its plan, that commissions background agents when it likes: builders for a separate piece, QA to review it like a player, or testers, on Lite or Ultra Flash. They show under the plan with their model, step, time and cost, and report back to the chat; a finished one wakes up for a follow-up. A watcher looks over the chat and its agents every 20 s and can block what one keeps doing; a stuck background agent gets one takeover. /crew 6 <task> allows 6 at once; /crew off ends it. /team is unchanged.

items.title: Directives
items.text: The watcher's instructions arrive as their own labelled message, can block what the agent keeps doing (check_page, a file it keeps re-reading, or everything but edits) for 8 steps, and must be acknowledged. Ignoring one twice hands the job over.

items.title: Follow-ups wake a finished helper
items.text: A helper that has finished stays idle until the main builder is done. Commissioning a job with its name again, or writing to it with team_say, wakes it in its own conversation, so it remembers its work; it reports back as before.

items.title: The researcher learns the topic
items.text: The researcher now researches the topic itself (how it works, its rules and real numbers, how it is usually built and what goes wrong) as well as what a great version needs; TEAM_SPEC.md has The topic, How it's built and the Checklist.

items.title: page_eval
items.text: Agents can run JavaScript in the live page (started, past its menus) and get the result: a value, a size, a WebGL error, or real pixel colours with screenPixels(), even on a WebGL canvas. For bugs an agent can't see.

items.title: A pointer when stuck
items.text: The second step in a row refused as a repeat says which tool gets new evidence: check_page with look_for to see, page_eval to measure, one change to test.

items.title: Repeated reasoning is a loop
items.text: An agent that writes the same reasoning again is told at once; the second time it gets a watcher note, the fourth time it is taken over.

items.title: One takeover per job
items.text: The takeover runs on Ultra Flash. If it gets stuck too, it is stopped and flagged as needing you, instead of handing over again.

releases.title: Agents that remember what they tried

items.title: An attempt log
items.text: Every edit, page check and command result is one line in a log yAI keeps; the last 30 lines go with every request of a team agent, where trimming never reaches, so it can see it already tried something.

items.title: Checks that compare
items.text: check_page starts with what changed since the agent's last check: the screen changed or not, new or fixed errors, the frame rate. A white page with text is no longer called blank.

items.title: Expected result first
items.text: Team agents say what a fix should change before making it, whether it did after checking, and what is different before trying again.

items.title: The page is checked
items.text: /crew found no page to open, so the browser check, playtest and performance check never ran: the page is now found from what the builder made, and the browser check and judge are always added for a web task.

items.title: QA reads like a player
items.text: QA reads the core files whole and walks through a session as a player would, instead of only the lines the project map points at.

items.title: Flip-flops caught
items.text: An edit that puts a file back to a version it already had is called out at once, with what to do instead; the board shows it.

items.title: The watcher can take over
items.text: An agent that keeps looping after a note from the watcher (or flip-flops 4 times after one) is stopped and its job handed to a fresh agent on Ultra with a hand-over: what is done, what the loop was, what to do instead. The watcher is also firmer: a loop gets a note the first time it is seen.

items.title: The builder plans its helpers
items.text: The main builder is asked to plan about 2 to 5 helpers early, so they work while it builds the core, and is reminded once if it has gone 4 minutes without one. The cap of 4 at once stays.

items.title: The builder picks each helper's model
items.text: commission takes <model>lite</model> for a simple, mechanical job (free) or flash, the default, for one that needs thought. The board shows which.

items.title: Faster page checks
items.text: check_page keeps one browser open per agent (data cleared and the cache off, so each check is a fresh visit), waits for the page instead of fixed times, measures the frame rate in half a second, and fetches the screen description in the background: it arrives with a later step unless look_for asks to see the screen first. An agent now waits about 3-4 s per check instead of 8-13 s.

items.title: Image order
items.text: Images go to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite first, then Groq (Qwen 3.8 27B), then Gemini 3.8 Flash, and never to Modal. With no image key set up, a clear error instead.

items.title: The watcher looks every 20 s
items.text: In /crew the watcher checks every 20 s so each agent's to-do list stays accurate, and steps in with a note or a stop at most once a minute.

items.title: A main builder with helpers
items.text: /crew <task>: one main builder (Ultra) builds the whole thing step by step, the way a single session does, and hands separate jobs (level data, sounds, sprites, tests, research) to helpers that work at the same time; their reports come back to it. The same checks, fixes, rounds and report as /team run after it. /crew 6 <task> lets up to 6 helpers work at once. /team is unchanged.

items.title: Fixer 2 carries on
items.text: When yAI's re-check still fails, fixer 2 continues in fixer 1's conversation with only what still fails, instead of starting over.

items.title: Page checks that see the game
items.text: check_page gets past difficulty and level menus, says plainly when the screen is blank or identical to the last check (and skips the description then), only re-runs for an agent after its own edit, and stores each picture once.

items.title: Progress checks
items.text: Every 8 minutes while builders work, yAI looks at the page against the request and tells the feed and the builders what is there and what is missing.

items.title: Where the time went
items.text: TEAM_REPORT.html has a table of each agent's steps (reads, edits, commands, page checks), refused repeats, watcher notes, restarts, tokens and the share cached, with what looks wasteful; the end summary shows the cache rate and the worst three.

items.title: One QA agent
items.text: A single QA check (the pieces fit, bugs, focused tests) replaces integration, tester and reviewer by default; they stay available on their own.

items.title: One to-do list for the fixer
items.text: The reports that found something are merged into one list, duplicates combined and worst first, before the fixer starts.

items.title: No waiting on one agent
items.text: When the rest of a stage is done and one agent runs well past them, it's told the team is waiting and to wrap up.

items.title: Later rounds check what changed
items.text: Round 2 and later bring back QA, the fixer, the spec score and the free checks, told which files the round changed; the narrower checks only when you ask for them.

items.title: Smaller briefs
items.text: With a long contract, each builder gets the parts that concern its feature and a list of where the rest is.

items.title: Real costs
items.text: After a tool call yAI reads on for a moment to get the real token counts and cost, instead of estimating them.

items.title: The watcher ticks the steps
items.text: Each agent's step list is updated from what it actually did, judged by the watcher, instead of waiting for the agent to say a step is done. Only an agent that finished well gets every step ticked; a failed or stopped one keeps what it really finished.

items.title: A closer watch
items.text: The watcher looks every 20 s instead of 75 s.

items.title: Fewer page checks
items.text: check_page isn't run again when nothing in the page's files changed; builders get the screen described on their first check and when they ask with look_for; agents are told to check after a group of changes, and the watcher looks out for over-checking.

items.title: Nothing hangs
items.text: Every browser call has a time limit and each built-in check an overall one; a frozen page is a failed check, not a run that never ends. A network restart, Esc or skip can no longer leave an agent working forever.

items.title: Stops mean stop
items.text: When today's allowance runs out the team stops like Esc; agents the watcher stops show as stopped; failures show as failed.

items.title: Money
items.text: Later rounds no longer pay for an extra fixer; the integration check is skipped when the page checks passed; long test runs are not mistaken for stuck agents; restarts keep their cost and files in the totals.

items.title: Reading
items.text: The already-read check only counts lines the agent was really shown, sees other agents' edits, and lets a summarized-away result be read again.

items.title: Faster failures
items.text: A host that refuses (quota, billing) is left out for the rest of the request: an image request that can't be served fails in 4 requests instead of 36. Network errors are retried only when they are network errors.

items.title: Sharper project map
items.text: Finds misspelt roots and calls and lowercase namespaces, ignores comments and shared setup lines, and never skips the merger for ES modules.

items.title: A watcher for the whole run
items.text: Every 75 s a cheap model reads what each working agent did lately and sends it a note when it is wasting time or going wrong, or stops one that keeps looping after a note. Its notes show in the feed and the agent's view.

items.title: No step limits, no automatic stops
items.text: Team agents have no step limit and are no longer stopped for repeating themselves; they are told, and the watcher decides.

items.title: Near-identical commands
items.text: The 5th command that starts the same way as 4 before it, with no file changed in between, is not run; the agent is told to change the code or finish.

items.title: Stopped means stopped
items.text: An agent stopped for looking without changing anything shows as failed, not done; and no role writes node -e harnesses for browser code.

items.title: Three free image models
items.text: Images go to Gemini 3.8 Flash, then Groq (Qwen 3.8 27B), then Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, then Modal. One whose free quota is used up passes straight to the next.

items.title: check_page waits less on the image model
items.text: The screen description gives up after 25 s and says so, so a check stays quick when the image model is down.

items.title: Why a fallback happened
items.text: When every host fails, the error now includes what the earlier ones said (for example Gemini before Modal).

items.title: Network drops are retried
items.text: A dropped connection or busy gateway before the reply starts is tried again up to 3 times.

items.title: No false ticks
items.text: An agent that ends on an error shows as failed, not done, and one that lost its connection is restarted automatically (twice at most).

items.title: Time limits on every page check
items.text: Pressing keys, reading the page, the screenshot and its description each have a time limit, and the whole check stops at 100 s. A page that hangs is reported as frozen instead of leaving the agent stuck on "opening it in a browser".

items.title: The merger only runs when needed
items.text: When yAI's own map of the code finds nothing that fails to line up, the merger is skipped. When it runs, it works from the list of mismatches instead of reading the whole project.

items.title: No more re-reading
items.text: A read of lines an agent already has (inside a range it read, still in the conversation, file unchanged) is not run again. An agent that reads 20 times without a change is told to act, and stopped at 32.

items.title: Progress that moves
items.text: After 6 steps on one plan step, the agent is asked whether that step is finished, so the board stops sitting on step 1.

items.title: Estimates from your own runs
items.text: Each role's real cost and time per model is remembered after a run, and the picker uses that average next time instead of a fixed guess.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash for images
items.text: Images go to Gemini 3.8 Flash instead of Flash-Lite, which missed a big first-person hand in a game screenshot.

items.title: Gemini reads the images
items.text: With GEMINI_API_KEY set, a message with an image (a photo on the website, a screenshot from check_page or the /team judge) goes to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite first, with Modal as the fallback. Text still goes to DeepSeek. DeepSeek's API is text-only, so images used to depend on Modal alone.

items.title: A lead that doesn't depend on Modal
items.text: The lead that splits a /team task and plans each round is yAI Ultra (DeepSeek V4 Pro), falling back to Ultra Flash, both on DeepSeek's own API. It used the partner model, yAI Q3.8 Max on Modal, and a Modal billing limit left a run waiting.

items.title: Rounds: build, play, improve
items.text: Set rounds with + and − in the picker (Showcase sets 3). After each round a judge plays it in a real browser and a model that can see compares it with your request; the lead then plans the next round from what is missing, what the judge saw and what still fails, and new feature builders improve it while the checks run again. It stops when the request is all done and the judge calls it good, the rounds run out, or the cost cap (twice the estimate) is reached. The bar shows each round with its score.

items.title: You in the loop
items.text: Between rounds the board waits up to 90 s: o opens it to play, what you type becomes the next round's first job, g goes on. In VS Code: Open it to play and Go on.

items.title: Researcher and skeleton check
items.text: A researcher searches the web for what a great version needs and writes TEAM_SPEC.md, a checklist with how to check each item, which everyone works to. After the architect, yAI opens the skeleton to make sure it runs before builders start.

items.title: Team chat
items.text: Agents can tell each other what affects them with team_say (to everyone or one agent); messages arrive after their next step, show in the live feed and transcripts, and agents that start later get the recent chat.

items.title: Snapshots and safety
items.text: Each round's files are saved in .yai-team/round-N. The picker warns when the estimate is more than today's allowance left; if it runs out mid-run the team stops with that reason instead of starting agents that are refused; an agent that never got to work shows as failed with why. Checkers are no longer switched on by browser features ("Web Audio API").

items.title: check_page
items.text: A new tool: open the web page or game in a real browser as it is right now, press its start button, hold keys (KeyW:1500), and get back errors, a frozen page, the frame rate, what the page says, and a plain, critical description of what is on screen from a model that can see it. Every /team agent is told to use it to see its work run.

items.title: /team splits by feature
items.text: The lead gives each builder a whole feature (mining and block cracks, mobs and combat, sound) instead of a file. A builder owns the files it creates and hooks into others' files with small exact edits; it can't overwrite another agent's file, so builders working at once never wipe each other's work.

items.title: The finish gate
items.text: After the fixer, a re-check row on the board: yAI itself re-runs the team's tests, opens the page, re-runs any of its own checks that failed, and plays the game again. If anything still fails, a second fixer round starts with only that evidence, then one more re-check, before the spec checker.

items.title: A score for the request
items.text: The spec checker ends with SCORE: done/asked, shown on the board, in the summary ("27 of 27 requirements done") and in the report.

items.title: Skeleton files
items.text: The architect starts every planned file as a skeleton with the shared names, ids and script tags; builders fill them in without renaming anything, so the pieces fit from the start.

items.title: TEAM_REPORT.html
items.text: Every run writes one self-contained page next to its contract: a replay of the board as it ran (play, speed, scrub), the stats, the requirement checklist, yAI's re-check, every agent with its model, time and cost, the playtest screenshots, the live feed and the files built.

items.title: Showcase preset
items.text: s in the picker (and in VS Code): every check that proves it works, yAI Ultra for the architect and spec checker, Ultra Flash for the rest.

items.title: Stuck agents restart themselves
items.text: An agent with no progress for 2 minutes is restarted once automatically; a second time it is flagged for you to retry or skip.

items.title: The playtester starts more games, and catches freezes
items.text: It now presses New World, Create World, Single player and Enter buttons too, and fails a game whose page stops answering after it starts (it used to play the title screen, and a game that froze on New World passed). A headless browser's pointer-lock error no longer counts against a game.

items.title: Fewer false leads in the project map
items.text: The map understands modules built as a private object and published (var Input = {…}; MC.Input = Input), members added later (Raycaster.cast = …) and fields set in methods (this.inv = …). On a Minecraft clone the false mismatches went from 11 to 0, while planted mistakes are still all caught.

items.title: A plan that can be read
items.text: On yAI Lite the lead that splits a /team task is yAI Ultra Flash (Lite wrote the plan as broken JSON and /team stopped with "Expected property name"). Small JSON mistakes in a plan are repaired, and a plan that still can't be read is asked for once more.

items.title: /team in the panel
items.text: The panel shows the same /team as the terminal: the picker (stages, a model per agent, estimates, Quick / Recommended / Everything, chat about the plan), then a live board with the stage bar, every agent's activity and progress, the live feed, and Retry / Skip on stuck agents. Click an agent to open it: its stats, steps, what it may change, its transcript, Pause and Restart.

items.title: Notes while yAI works
items.text: You can send while yAI is busy: it reads your note after its current step (during /team it goes to the whole team, or the agent you opened, and shows when it was read). With the box empty the button still stops yAI.

items.title: Plan card and tables
items.text: yAI's plan shows above the composer while it works, ticked off step by step, and Markdown tables in answers are drawn as tables.

items.title: Notes to agents show up
items.text: A note you send to a /team agent (or the whole team) appears in its view at once, marked as waiting until its current step ends, then ✓ read; the live feed says when it read it.

items.title: No more 2-minute scripts
items.text: A team agent's node -e script stops after 30 s instead of 120 s, with a hint that browser code never finishes in Node; the merger is told not to write such scripts at all.

releases.title: Team agents can look things up

items.title: Services and MCP for /team
items.text: Every /team agent can now use your connected services that only read (Wolfram Alpha, weather, maps, stocks, sports, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, YouTube) and your MCP servers' read-only tools, besides web search and fetch, and is told when to reach for them. Services and MCP tools that change something (a Discord or Slack post, a webhook, a GitHub issue, an n8n workflow) stay with you.

items.title: Wide windows
items.text: The /team screens use the whole window instead of stopping at 140 columns; on a wide window the live feed gets a third of it and agent names more room.

items.title: Pick your team
items.text: The agents are laid out as stages (Plan, Build, Join, Check, Fix), each with its model (← → to change it) and an estimate of its time and cost. Presets on q, r and e (Quick, Recommended, Everything); the Start box shows the whole run's estimated time and cost; c talks the plan over instead of starting.

items.title: The team at work
items.text: A bar of the stages on top, then every agent under its stage with what it is doing in plain words, a progress bar from its own plan, its time and cost. A live feed down the right shows hand-offs, problems found, agents finishing or stuck, and your notes. A stuck agent can be retried (r) or skipped (s); ↑↓ and enter open any agent.

items.title: Watching one agent
items.text: Tabs for every agent, and a side panel with its stage and model, time, tokens and cost, its steps, what it may change and who waits on it, next to its transcript. Tab moves to the next agent, p pauses it after its current step, r restarts a stuck one.

items.title: Talk to the team
items.text: What you type while a team runs goes to every working agent (and to the ones that start later); while you watch one agent, it goes to that agent only.

items.title: A map of the project
items.text: Before the merger, integration, reviewer, fixer and spec checker start, yAI maps the project itself, at no cost: what each file defines and where, and the names that don't line up (a name one file uses and no file defines, with the likely intended name; one defined twice; an element id no page has; a script that doesn't exist). They start from the map and read only the lines they need, so they no longer run out of memory on big projects.

items.title: Line ranges
items.text: read_file takes a line range in the path (js/world.js:120-180), several at once. A long file read whole isn't read whole again unless it changed; the agent is pointed to the lines it needs, and a search for everything (.*) is refused.

items.title: Fixer and tests
items.text: The fixer keeps what the team contract promises. After it, yAI always re-runs the team's own test suite, not only the single test files the agents ran.

items.title: Fallbacks on the board
items.text: An agent whose replies came partly from the fallback model (yAI Lite busy, so DeepSeek Flash answered) shows how many, for example Lite (3 via fallback).

items.title: Tidier agent views
items.text: What an agent says is no longer cut into lines before the team view wraps it, so sentences don't break in the middle. A stopped team agent no longer suggests /model.

items.title: Each role starts on a suggested model
items.text: yAI Ultra for the architect; yAI Lite for the builders, designer, docs, api and setup; yAI Ultra Flash for the merger, integration, tester, reviewer, security, fixer and spec checker, which read the whole project. A model that is not available falls to the next one. Change any of them with ← → in the picker; your picks are remembered.

items.title: Merger and checkers keep more in mind
items.text: The /team roles that must see the whole project at once (merger, integration, reviewer, fixer, spec checker) keep up to 80k tokens of file contents before old ones are trimmed, up from 48k. On big projects they had been losing the first files while reading the last, re-reading them until they were stopped.

items.title: Agents listed in the order they run
items.text: The architect is listed first, then the builders, the merger and designer, yAI's own checks, the checkers, the fixer and the spec checker. An agent that hasn't started shows no time instead of the whole team's.

items.title: Every /team report in one shape
items.text: Agents end with the same short report: a Report heading, then labelled sections (Changed, Problems, Checks, For the others, Left to do) of one-sentence bullets with the file and line. The agent view and /team log draw it with bold labels, bullets that wrap neatly, files highlighted and the verdict as a coloured label.

items.title: One summary instead of every report
items.text: When a /team run ends you get one aligned block: what was built, every check's verdict, what the fixer changed and whether the re-run tests pass, and a list of anything that needs a look. The reports are no longer printed one after another; /team log shows any agent's whole report, and yAI still has them all for follow-up questions.

items.title: Built-in checks are labelled
items.text: In the /team picker, yAI's own browser checks (mobile, performance, accessibility, playtester) say built-in in the model column, since they use no AI model.

items.title: Pick each agent's model
items.text: In the /team picker, ← → changes the model of the highlighted agent: for example yAI Ultra for the architect and fixer, and yAI Lite for the builders. The picks are remembered per role, and the board shows each agent's model next to its cost.

items.title: Unticking a builder
items.text: Unticking a builder in the /team picker now always leaves out that builder; with an architect on the team it could leave out a different one.

items.title: yAI Lite by default
items.text: yAI Lite (GLM-4.7 Flash, free) is the default model on the website, in yAI Code and for API calls that name no model. When it is busy the reply comes from DeepSeek Flash instead.

items.title: yAI P4 removed
items.text: yAI P4 (Phi 4 Mini) is no longer offered. yAI Q3.5 stays as the model on the host PC.

items.title: yAI Lite (GLM-4.7 Flash)
items.text: A free model on Z.ai's own API, for quick questions and light coding. When the free model is busy it moves to GLM-4.7 FlashX (a few cents per million tokens), then DeepSeek Flash. Past your daily allowance it keeps working on the free model alone. Text only.

items.title: Markdown tables line up
items.text: A table in a reply, an agent view or a /team report is drawn with aligned columns and a header rule instead of raw | pipes. Cells too wide for the terminal wrap inside their column.

items.title: No more home-screen widgets
items.text: The home-screen widget page, its private links and its menu entries are gone. App shortcuts and links that start a question (?q=…) still work.

items.title: No more ** and backticks in /team
items.text: Watching an agent, and the reports at the end of a team, now show bold, code and lists formatted like the main view instead of the raw ** and ` symbols, and long lines no longer leave a single word on a line of its own.

items.title: Steps work on yAI Ultra and Ultra Flash
items.text: On DeepSeek’s API the models can’t write their tool-call markup as plain text, so they wrote look-alikes that yAI Code didn’t recognise and steps didn’t run. yAI Code now sends its tools through DeepSeek’s documented function-calling interface and gets each step back in its usual form. Modal works as before.

releases.title: yAI Ultra is now DeepSeek V4 Pro

items.title: A new yAI Ultra
items.text: yAI Ultra runs on DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of Kimi K3, at a fifth of the price or less (half again outside DeepSeek’s peak hours), so your daily allowance goes much further. Messages with images still go to Kimi K3, since DeepSeek’s API reads text only, and Kimi K3 steps in if DeepSeek is unavailable. Saved picks, scheduled tasks and API keys that name the old model keep working.

items.title: Steps run again on yAI Ultra Flash
items.text: Through DeepSeek’s own API the model writes its tool calls with doubled bars, which yAI Code didn’t recognise, so it showed the markup instead of running the step. Both forms work now.

items.title: Cheaper Ultra Flash
items.text: When a DeepSeek API key is set, yAI Ultra Flash runs on DeepSeek’s own API: cached input costs a fifth of what it did, and outside DeepSeek’s peak hours everything is half price. Modal stays as the fallback, and messages with images still go to Modal. The daily allowance counts the price of whichever one answered.

items.title: Builders build, checkers test
items.text: In a chess run, builders wrote their files in a few steps, then spent 40 to 100 more printing pieces of them with node -e and writing _test.js harnesses. Builders are now told to write, run one syntax check, and finish, and to leave testing to the tester. A team agent that has made its changes and then takes 15 steps without changing anything is told to finish; at 25 it is stopped, keeping its work.

items.title: Tidier agent view and command boxes
items.text: Watching an agent no longer shows big gaps between steps, and a command written over several lines (node -e “…”) stays on one row instead of breaking the view. The “Run this command?” boxes show such a command line by line inside the box.

items.title: Pasted commands work
items.text: A long paste shows as [Pasted text #1] in the prompt, so a pasted “/team …” was sent to the model as a message instead of starting the team. Pasted commands now run as commands, “/team ” followed by a paste works too, and a /team task pasted over several lines is joined into one.

releases.title: The spec checker sees the fixed version

items.title: Page re-opened before the spec check
items.text: After the fixer, yAI opens the page again before the spec checker starts, and the spec checker is told the earlier browser check is out of date. Before, it judged a fixed game by the errors from before the fix.

items.title: No more read, trim, read again
items.text: A /team reviewer read the whole game, had it trimmed to save space, read it again, had it trimmed again, and hit the step limit. Team agents now trim only past about 48k tokens, never cut their last 8 steps, and may re-read something that was trimmed once, not again and again.

items.title: Costs shown with the prompt cache
items.text: Most steps end at a tool call, before the site sends the real cost, so yAI Code estimated it, counting the whole conversation at full price. The part already sent last time is now counted at the cached price (a tenth), so the board shows what a run really costs, about a third of what it showed before.

items.title: Read several files in one step
items.text: read_file takes up to 8 paths, one per line. Each step re-sends the whole conversation, so reading 7 files in one step instead of 7 saves 6 re-sends.

items.title: Leaner team agents
items.text: /team agents get a short system prompt of their own (about half the size), are told not to re-read their brief or the contract, and once an agent passes about 28k tokens its old tool output is cut in one go. A long contract is cut at a line and says where the rest starts.

items.title: Fewer AI checkers
items.text: yAI’s own browser checks (mobile, performance, accessibility, playtester) now run first and cost almost nothing. The integration check is done by the reviewer when both are on, and skipped when the page opened cleanly and every built-in check passed. The AI checkers see the built-in results.

releases.title: No more agents going round in circles

items.title: Repeated steps are caught
items.text: If yAI asks to read the same file, list the same folder or run the same command again when nothing has changed, it isn’t done twice: yAI is told it already has the answer. After three repeats it is told to make its change or finish, and after six it is stopped. In a test run, one /team builder had re-read the same file 43 times and written nothing.

items.title: Team agents that write get 100 steps
items.text: Builders, the merger, the designer and the fixer can now take up to 100 steps instead of 50, so a fixer no longer stops halfway through a fix. The board shows “stuck · stopped” or “hit the step limit” in yellow when that happens.

items.title: Architect, merger, designer and spec checker
items.text: In /team, an architect can design how the pieces fit before anyone builds (a detailed contract every builder follows), a merger joins the builders' pieces, a designer polishes the look (CSS only), and a spec checker goes through your request item by item at the very end.

items.title: API and setup checkers
items.text: An API checker starts the server, calls every route with good and bad input and checks the answers; a setup checker makes sure it runs from a clean checkout (imports, dependencies, file-name case, README steps, no secrets).

items.title: Checks yAI runs in a real browser
items.text: Mobile (phone, tablet and laptop sizes: sideways scrolling, cut-off areas, tiny buttons), performance (load time, page weight, frame rate, freezes), accessibility (axe-core rules and keyboard use) and a playtester that plays a game for 30 seconds, through game over and Play again, and checks saved scores survive a reload. The checklist groups everyone by when they run, with sensible defaults for the task.

releases.title: A team that checks the controls

items.title: /team tries the controls
items.text: For games, the browser check now holds the arrow keys (or WASD) and sweeps the mouse across the game, then a model that can see compares the screenshots. Dead keys or a dead mouse fail the check, and the page is checked again after the fixer.

items.title: No more explaining away a failing check
items.text: The fixer must re-run the existing tests and re-check every control after its edits, and any check it or the tester changes has to be listed with the reason. Read-only checkers can run several safe checks in one go, the contract can no longer take browser built-ins like Audio, briefs count builders correctly, the test re-run skips commands that never started, and /team warns when yAI Code is running in your home folder.

items.title: Focus on a company or project
items.text: Put a knowledge file in ~/.yai/packs/<name>.md (its people, systems, folders and rules) and yAI Code keeps it in front of the model for the whole session: /focus <name> or just /<name> turns it on, yai <name> starts in its folder with it on, and it can switch itself on whenever yAI Code starts in that folder. The header shows which focus is on. Packs stay on your PC.

items.title: A home-screen widget
items.text: The new Widgets page sets up a daily brief widget: your weather, LEARN due dates, the latest scheduled task and whether a PC is live in Remote. On iPhone it runs in the free Scriptable app (the script is ready to copy, with your private link in it); on Android any web-widget app can show it.

items.title: Shortcuts and quick-ask links
items.text: Long-press the installed app for New chat, Ask by voice, Remote and Scheduled. Links like /?q=your question open yAI and ask straight away, handy for iOS Shortcuts and launchers.

items.title: On a new branch, then push
items.text: Pick "On a new branch, then push" when you send a task from Remote: your PC does the work on a new branch, commits it, pushes it, and goes back to the branch it was on, so you can review it later. Your phone gets a notification when any Remote task finishes.

items.title: Live weather, stock and score cards
items.text: Ask about the weather, a stock or crypto price, or tonight's games, and a live card sits above the answer: the forecast for the week, the price with today's chart, or the scores with team logos. Cards update themselves while they're on screen (scores and prices every 30 seconds).

items.title: Hover a citation
items.text: Hover (or tap) a [1] in an answer to see the source and the exact sentence from it that backs the claim.

items.title: Check this
items.text: Check under an answer pulls out its facts, searches each one and shows which the sources support, doubt or contradict, with links.

items.title: Another answer, side by side
items.text: Another asks the same model again and shows both answers next to each other. Keep the one you like.

items.title: Slides from a chat
items.text: Slides turns the conversation into a deck you can preview and save as PowerPoint or PDF.

items.title: Price and page watchers
items.text: On the Scheduled page (or by asking in a chat), watch a product page for a price drop or under a price you set, or any page for changes. yAI checks it every 1, 6 or 24 hours and sends a notification (and a webhook if you like) with what changed.

items.title: Remote looks like a yAI chat
items.text: Run on your PC is now Remote. Each run of yai remote is a session: the live one at the top with a green dot, past ones below. Open one to see it as a chat: your tasks as messages, yAI's replies, its steps with results, its edits as diffs you can open, and its questions as buttons. Send the next task from the box at the bottom; tasks in a session remember what came before. Output is now kept for a week.

items.title: A contract for every /team
items.text: The lead now writes down every name the files share (functions, element ids, events) in TEAM_CONTRACT.md, and every agent gets it word for word, so one file can no longer call render while another defines renderWorld.

items.title: yAI opens web work in a browser
items.text: For pages and games, yAI loads the page in a headless browser after the builders, presses Start, and reports console errors, failed loads, a blank canvas and what the screenshot looks like. The fixer gets that, and the page is checked again after it.

items.title: Tidier teams
items.text: Notes the builders leave for each other go to the integration agent and the fixer. Old files in the folder can be moved aside first, a stopped team offers to remove what it made, files made outside the plan are listed, and testers check whether a failing test is itself wrong.

items.title: More agents when you want them
items.text: /team 6 … or asking for as many agents as possible now allows up to 8 builders. Files are also read in bigger pieces (600 lines), so follow-up fixes take fewer steps.

items.title: Live steps instead of dots
items.text: While yAI looks things up, the reply shows each step as it happens (Checking the weather in Waterloo, ON · Searching arXiv for …), with a tick when each is done.

items.title: Plain-words steps
items.text: Connections in yAI Code show the same words while they run, in the spinner and the step row.

items.title: Spotify and Google Drive removed
items.text: The Spotify and Google Drive and Docs connections are gone; GitHub, LEARN, webhooks, weather, maps, Wolfram Alpha, papers and YouTube stay. Google sign-in goes back to asking only for calendar and email.

items.title: Connections
items.text: yAI can now use outside services when a question needs them: live weather, maps and directions, Wolfram Alpha, arXiv and Semantic Scholar papers, YouTube transcripts, and your own GitHub, Google Drive and Docs, Spotify and UWaterloo LEARN due dates. Open Connections in the account menu to connect them. Answers say which ones were used, with sources.

items.title: Actions wait for you
items.text: Anything that changes something (a Spotify playlist, a GitHub issue, a Google Doc, a webhook message) comes as a card with a Do it button, and only happens when you press it.

items.title: Webhooks
items.text: Save webhooks (Discord, Slack, Zapier, n8n, any URL) under Connections. yAI can send to them, and scheduled tasks can send their results there too. Scheduled tasks also use your connected services, so "every Sunday, tell me what is due on LEARN" works.

items.title: Connections in the terminal
items.text: The same services reach yAI Code through its service tool. New commands: /connections, /pr (push and open a pull request written from the diff), /issues (pick a GitHub issue and let yAI work on it) and /deploy (a Vercel preview or production, with a fix offer if the build fails).

items.title: /team plans the layout first
items.text: The lead now plans every file and its owner up front. yAI makes the folders before anyone starts, and every agent gets the whole map in its brief.

items.title: Live previews no longer stop at "Script error"
items.text: Code that saves data (localStorage) or uses cookies now runs in the preview, the way it does when opened in the browser. Errors from scripts loaded from the big CDNs show the real message and line instead of "Script error.".

items.title: No verdict is a warning
items.text: In /team, a checker that finishes without its verdict now shows "no verdict" in yellow with a warning that its check may be incomplete, and the fixer gets its report to look at.

items.title: yAI re-runs the tests after the fixer
items.text: When the fixer is done, yAI runs the test commands the team used (or npm test) itself and shows the real result next to the fixer's verdict, with a warning if it said FIXED but the tests still fail. The fixer is also told to quote each check it ran with its result.

items.title: Open any agent in /team
items.text: While a team works, press an agent's number on the board, or click its row, to watch it live: what it says, each step and its result, and its file edits as coloured diffs. Esc goes back to the board (Esc on the board still stops the team).

items.title: /team log
items.text: After a team finishes, /team log 2 (or /team log tester) prints that agent's whole log into the conversation.

releases.title: Copy and paste in yAI Code

items.title: Select to copy
items.text: Drag over any text in yAI Code to select it; it is copied when you let go, as in Claude Code. A selection stays inside the conversation or the plan panel, and wrapped lines come back together.

items.title: Pasting
items.text: Pasted text no longer sends the prompt at its line breaks. A short line goes in as typed; anything longer shows as [Pasted text #1 +N lines] and the whole text goes to the model.

items.title: /team questions stay on screen
items.text: When a team agent asks to run a command, its question no longer flashes and disappears: the live board waits until you answer.

items.title: Tester, reviewer, security checker, docs writer and fixer in /team
items.text: After the builders finish, the members you picked check the work together: the integration agent (do the pieces fit), a tester (writes and runs tests), a reviewer (bugs and edge cases), a security checker and a docs writer. Each ends with a verdict. If any of them finds a problem, the fixer runs last with their reports, fixes it and re-runs the checks; if nothing is found it is skipped.

items.title: Choose who is on the team
items.text: After the lead splits the task, a checklist shows the builders and every role: tick or untick with space or a number, then Start. Your picks are remembered for next time. The verdicts are summed up in one line when the team finishes.

items.title: Searches the web when it needs to
items.text: Without pressing Search, yAI checks whether your question needs the web (news, prices, anything recent or obscure, or when you ask it to look something up) and searches on its own, with sources as usual. Coding, maths and writing questions go straight to the answer.

items.title: Yolo mode
items.text: Shift+Tab now also offers auto-accept everything: edits, commands and deletions run without asking (/mode yolo). In /team the builders follow it too.

items.title: An integration agent in /team
items.text: After the agents finish, an integration agent checks, read-only, that their pieces fit together: imports exist, names and routes match, nothing is left half-wired. Its verdict comes last in the report.

items.title: A plan you can trust
items.text: The plan's progress now counts finished steps, not tool calls, never goes backwards, and is complete when a task ends well.

items.title: Ultra Flash tool calls
items.text: yAI Ultra Flash now writes its tool calls in its own native format, so steps are no longer thrown away as unfinished.

items.title: No more jumping screen
items.text: Typing (backspace included) only redraws what changed, inside one update, and nothing touches the window's last column, so a wide symbol can't push a row over and make the whole screen jump.

items.title: /team tidies up
items.text: The agents' board no longer comes back under the reports after the team is done.

items.title: Resizing
items.text: After the window gets narrower, boxes and right-aligned rows are cut at the edge instead of breaking into pieces.

releases.title: yAI Code asks before it guesses

items.title: Questions in a small form
items.text: When a task has real choices the code can't answer (a fixed list or free text? one field or several?), yAI asks up to four questions in a form: a tab for each, numbered options with a line under each, Type something for your own answer, and Chat about this to talk it over. The Submit tab shows your answers before they go.

items.title: A full-window app, like the design
items.text: The header with the status pill stays at the top, the plan sits in a panel on the right while yAI works, and the input box and the keys that work right now stay at the bottom. PgUp/PgDn or the mouse wheel scroll back through the conversation. YAI_CLASSIC=1 brings back the plain scrolling terminal.

items.title: Ready to type straight away
items.text: MCP servers start in the background, so the input works at once; a message waits for them if it needs their tools.

items.title: Cleaner start
items.text: The start screen sits in the middle of the window and gives way to the conversation; "pick up where you left off" shows a clean title.

items.title: Always know what it is doing
items.text: A status pill says Ready, Working, Finished or Needs attention, and while yAI works its plan stays at the bottom with each step ticked off and the files it changed.

items.title: Plain-language start
items.text: Instead of a wall of tips: what yAI saw in the project and four starters (fix something, add a feature, explain the project, review changes), each a single key, and R to pick up the last conversation.

items.title: One-key answers
items.text: Approvals say what a command does and how risky it is (read-only, changes files, network, risky) and take y, a or n. When a task is done you get a summary and r, c or u to review, commit or undo it all.

items.title: Failures in plain words
items.text: When a test fails, yAI explains it simply before the stack trace and offers f to fix it, s to see the fix first, or n to leave it.

items.title: Commands with descriptions
items.text: Typing / shows matching commands with what each does and what is on now; arrows move, tab completes, and the bar under the input lists the keys that work right now.

items.title: Hosted models labelled right
items.text: yAI Q3.8 Max now shows as Hosted in the model picker.

items.title: Opens on the logo
items.text: The phone app opens on the yAI logo, which settles in while your chats load, then fades into the app.

items.title: A bigger start screen
items.text: The start box shows yAI in large letters with the version and tagline on one line, like the videos.

items.title: /team: agents that split the work
items.text: A lead splits the task into 2 to 4 parts that touch different files, and the agents do them at the same time while a live board shows each one's step, time and cost. Commands still ask you first. Their reports land in your conversation.

items.title: Fewer failed steps with yAI Ultra Flash
items.text: In long sessions Ultra Flash sometimes wrote its tool calls slightly wrong (a missing quote), so steps failed with "a path is required" and had to be redone. Those calls are now understood the first time.

items.title: Model arena removed
items.text: The arena and its leaderboard are gone; the phone app has three tabs: Chats, Projects and You.

items.title: Diagrams, charts and formulas
items.text: Charts and diagrams redraw in the right colours when you switch light or dark, wide diagrams stay readable on a phone, and a long formula shows a shadow where it scrolls.

items.title: No more surprise keyboard
items.text: Turning on a tool from the + menu (search, deep research, study, canvas) or tapping a start suggestion no longer pops the keyboard; only tapping the message box does.

items.title: Tidier layouts
items.text: Wide diagrams stay readable and scroll sideways, long project names are cut off neatly instead of wrapping, and the theme buttons are easier to tap.

items.title: Scheduled tasks
items.text: Tell yAI to do something every day, on weekdays, every week or once, at a time you pick (for example a morning news briefing with web search). Each result is saved as a chat marked ⏰ and sent to your phone or browser as a notification. Find it under Scheduled in the sidebar.

items.title: Diagrams and charts in answers
items.text: When a picture explains it better, answers include diagrams (flows, sequences, timelines) and charts (bar, line, area, pie, scatter) with a table view and a download button.

items.title: Prompt caching
items.text: The repeated part of a conversation is cached by the model, so follow-up messages are faster and cost up to 80% less from your daily allowance. Your usage page shows the tokens served from cache.

items.title: Fits your window
items.text: Resizing the terminal redraws at the new width, and file searches and reads show a spinner with a timer.

releases.title: A much bigger yAI Q3.8 Max

items.title: yAI Q3.8 Max is now Qwen3.8 Max
items.text: The 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8 Max replaces the 27B model. It answers right away instead of waiting for a cloud GPU to wake, and like yAI Ultra it counts toward your daily allowance (about half of Ultra's price). It reads text only; for images use yAI Ultra or yAI Ultra Flash.

releases.title: yAI on your phone, as an app

items.title: Three tabs
items.text: Chats, Projects and You, with the tabs out of the way inside a conversation.

items.title: Sheets for models and tools
items.text: Tap the model under the chat title to switch, and + for Camera, Photos, Files, Search, Research, Image, Video, Study, Canvas and Voice.

items.title: Feels native
items.text: Swipe from the left edge or use your phone's back button to go back, a full-screen live preview, and a Settings screen with Light, Dark or System theme.

items.title: yAI Ultra Flash
items.text: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: fast, reads images, no GPU to wake, and about a tenth of yAI Ultra's price per word. It shares yAI Ultra's daily allowance, so the same dollars go about ten times further.

items.title: Voice mode
items.text: Speak instead of typing with the mic, press Listen under any answer, or start a hands-free voice chat. Natural voices when the site has them, your browser's voice otherwise.

items.title: Canvas
items.text: Long writing and code open in an editor beside the chat. Edit by hand, select a part and ask yAI to change it, step through versions, and run HTML, JavaScript and Python live.

items.title: Search your chats
items.text: Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) searches every chat's messages, and jumps to the exact message. New chat moved to Ctrl Shift O.

items.title: Study mode
items.text: A tutor that gives hints and asks questions instead of handing over answers (Tools > Study mode), plus a Study page with flashcards (spaced repetition) and practice quizzes made from your notes, PDFs or chats.

items.title: Calendar and email
items.text: Connect Google to ask about your week and your inbox. yAI suggests Gmail drafts and calendar events; nothing is saved until you press the button.

items.title: Better image editing
items.text: An Edit button on every image yAI makes, one-tap ideas (remove the background, watercolor, winter...), and a before/after slider.

items.title: Install yAI as an app
items.text: Account menu > Install the app (or Add to Home Screen on an iPhone). It opens full screen with its own icon.

items.title: Public API keys
items.text: Call yAI's models from your own code with an OpenAI-style API at /v1, under your own daily limits. Keys are on the API keys page.

items.title: VS Code extension, /resume, plan approval
items.text: yAI Code in a VS Code side panel with changes shown as diffs; /resume picks any earlier session; plan mode ends with a plan you approve.

items.title: Live cost, /compact, image to code, run from your phone
items.text: The status line shows what yAI Ultra has cost this session and today; /compact takes a focus; /clone rebuilds a page from a screenshot; yai remote takes tasks from your phone.

items.title: People and limits
items.text: Admins see everyone's use, change each person's daily limits, pause accounts, and get automatic flags for unusual use.

releases.title: Data analysis, deep research and memory

items.title: Data analysis
items.text: Attach a CSV, Excel or JSON file; Python runs in your browser and the charts show in the chat.

items.title: Deep research
items.text: Several rounds of searching and reading, then a report with sources.

items.title: Memory
items.text: yAI remembers lasting facts you tell it; edit them in Account > Memory.

items.title: Paste screenshots and /usage
items.text: Alt+V pastes a screenshot into the prompt; /usage shows today's limits.

items.title: A new look
items.text: New colours and type, a sidebar that folds into a rail, and a new usage page.

items.title: yAI Code redesign
items.text: Dark and light themes, a start screen, step rows, diffs and arrow-key approvals.

items.title: New model names
items.text: yAI Ultra, yAI Q3.8 Max, yAI 3 Coder, yAI Q3.5 and yAI P4.

items.title: Search the web
items.text: Answers with numbered sources.

items.title: Projects
items.text: Files and instructions shared by every chat in a project.

items.title: Live previews
items.text: Run the HTML and JavaScript yAI writes, right in the chat.

items.title: Usage page
items.text: See what you've used.
